Every value below was read out of the render that produced this page.
The filter is enabled in this site's `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
filters:
  - path: lua-env
    at: pre-quarto
```

## Pandoc

| Source | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `{{{< lua-env pandoc.FORMAT >}}}` | {{< lua-env pandoc.FORMAT >}} |
| `{{{< lua-env pandoc.PANDOC_VERSION >}}}` | {{< lua-env pandoc.PANDOC_VERSION >}} |
| `{{{< lua-env pandoc.PANDOC_API_VERSION >}}}` | {{< lua-env pandoc.PANDOC_API_VERSION >}} |

: Pandoc globals, as this page was written. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[55,45]"}

Render the same document to another format and `pandoc.FORMAT` changes with it.

| Source | Value |

## Through the `meta` shortcode

Everything sits under the `lua-env` metadata key as well, so Quarto's own shortcode reaches it without the extension's own:

| Source | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `{{{< meta lua-env.pandoc.FORMAT >}}}` | {{< meta lua-env.pandoc.FORMAT >}} |

: The same value, read as ordinary metadata. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[55,45]"}

::: {.callout-note}
The two shortcodes are not interchangeable.
`meta` prints scalars, and reports `?invalid meta type` for anything else, so a path such as `lua-env.quarto.version`, which is a list of three numbers, needs the extension's own shortcode.
:::

## Exporting to JSON

This site leaves the export off, since it would write host paths into a file the site then publishes:

```yaml
extensions:
  lua-env:
    json: false
```

Turning it on writes `lua-env.json` beside the source document, so add it to `.gitignore`:

```yaml
extensions:
  lua-env:
    json: true
```

Narrow it to what you actually want, and the file stays readable:

```yaml
extensions:
  lua-env:
    json: true
    json-include:
      - pandoc.FORMAT
      - quarto.version
```

Or keep everything except one noisy branch:

```yaml
extensions:
  lua-env:
    json: true
    json-exclude:
      - quarto._quarto
```

::: {.callout-warning}
`json-exclude-sensitive` defaults to `true` and drops the input file, the output file, the project directories, and the Pandoc script path.
Leave it on unless the file stays on your own machine.
:::
